q: Which pillar of Islam is Zakat?
facts: • The standard order is Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.
Sawm (fasting in Ramadan) is the fourth pillar.

q: What is the x-coordinate of a point called in analytic geometry?
facts: • The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
In (x, y), the abscissa is the first coordinate and the ordinate the second. Primary / official reference

q: On what date did the five daily prayers become obligatory in Islamic tradition?
ans: During the Mi'raj, traditionally dated to 27 Rajab in some calendars; the exact date is disputed
facts: • The obligation is associated with the Night Journey and Ascension.
Avoid treating 27 Rajab/10 Nabawi as an agreed historical date across all sources.

q: In which sea is the Gulf of Riga located?
facts: • The Gulf of Riga lies between Latvia and Estonia.
Riga, Latvia's capital, is at the gulf's southern end.

q: What is the highest military order of the Netherlands?
facts: • It is the Netherlands' highest and oldest order for military bravery.
The order was established in 1815.

q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located?
ans: Punjab, near Kalabagh in Mianwali District
facts: • The proposed dam site is on the Indus River.
It remains a controversial project and should not be confused with the operational Tarbela Dam.

q: Which Caliph was Hazrat Umar (RA)?
facts: • Umar (RA) succeeded Abu Bakr (RA).
His caliphate is commonly dated 634–644 CE.

q: In which direction is India from Pakistan?
facts: • Pakistan's eastern border is with India.
The international boundary includes the Radcliffe Line across much of Punjab and adjoining areas.

q: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
facts: • The treaty was concluded between the Muslims of Madinah and Quraysh of Makkah.
It created a period of truce and preceded the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

q: What type of government did Pakistan's 1962 Constitution establish?
facts: • The Constitution was introduced under Ayub Khan.
The 1973 Constitution re-established a parliamentary system.

q: Where is the shrine of Mian Mir located?
facts: • Mian Mir was a revered Sufi associated with Lahore.
Tradition connects him with the Sikh Guru Arjan, although historical details vary by source.

q: Haba Khatoon was a poet of which language?
facts: • Haba Khatoon was a Kashmiri poet and queen, traditionally associated with Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak.
She is celebrated for Kashmiri lyric poetry.

q: How many centres does a circle have?
facts: • All points on a circle are equidistant from its centre.
The radius is the distance from the centre to the circumference.

q: Which rivers were allocated to Pakistan under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty?
ans: The western rivers: Indus, Jhelum and Chenab
facts: • The eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej were allocated primarily to India under the treaty.
The World Bank played a role in facilitating the agreement signed in 1960. Primary / official reference

q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka?
facts: • Colombo is the commercial capital; Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the legislative capital.
The currency is divided into 100 cents.

q: What is another name for the 1940 Lahore Resolution?
facts: • It was passed at the Muslim League session in Lahore on 23 March 1940.
It was a resolution, not a constitution.

q: What is Pakistan's national flower?
facts: • Jasmine is the commonly recognized national flower.
The answer is the same whether the question asks for Pakistan's national flower or “national floral emblem” in common GK.

q: Which part of Pakistan borders China?
ans: Gilgit-Baltistan, not a province in Pakistan's constitutional structure
facts: • The border is reached through Khunjerab Pass into China's Xinjiang region.
Pakistan's four provinces are Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

q: What is the capital of Belarus?
facts: • Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.
Its currency is the Belarusian ruble.

q: On which continent is Lake Victoria?
facts: • It is shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
It is Africa's largest lake by surface area.

q: What is the world's smallest ocean by area?
facts: • The Arctic Ocean is largely surrounded by North America and Eurasia.
It is also the shallowest of the five commonly recognized oceans.

q: When was the Lucknow Pact signed?
facts: • The pact was reached by Congress and the Muslim League.
It included agreement on separate electorates and political representation.

q: Where are the Ras Koh Hills located?
facts: • Pakistan conducted its 1998 nuclear tests in the Ras Koh region.
Do not confuse Ras Koh with the Kirthar Range in Sindh/Balochistan.

q: In which country is the Port of Rotterdam located?
facts: • Rotterdam is one of Europe's major ports.
The port connects maritime trade with the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt delta and inland Europe.

q: What is the approximate length of the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor from Kashgar to Gwadar?
facts: • CPEC links Xinjiang in China to Gwadar Port in Balochistan.
It includes road, rail, energy and logistics projects; route details vary by corridor alignment.

q: What is the height of Ras Koh's highest peak?
ans: The supplied figure of about 3,010 m is not sufficiently verified; use only with a reliable geographic source
facts: • Ras Koh is a mountain range in Balochistan's Chagai region.
It is known in Pakistan's geography/current-affairs context because of the 1998 nuclear tests.

q: What is the publicly stated range of Pakistan's Nasr missile?
ans: Often reported as about 70 km; specifications are source-dependent
facts: • Nasr (Hatf-IX) is described by Pakistan as a short-range tactical ballistic missile.
Military performance figures should be attributed to an official statement or reputable defence source.

q: Where is the OIC headquarters located?
facts: • The OIC was established in 1969.
It has member states across Africa, Asia and other regions.

q: What does the title Dhun-Nurayn for Hazrat Usman (RA) mean?
facts: • The title is linked in Islamic tradition to his marriages to two daughters of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in succession.
Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Caliph.

q: What title is traditionally associated with Prophet Ismail (AS) in sacrifice narratives?
ans: Dhabihullah (the one offered for sacrifice), in traditional usage
facts: • The Qur'an recounts the test of sacrifice without naming the son in the relevant verses; Muslim tradition generally identifies him as Ismail (AS).
The exact honorific is a traditional religious title, not a Qur'anic proper name.

q: Which German general was nicknamed the “Desert Fox”?
facts: • Rommel commanded German forces in North Africa during World War II.
The nickname is associated with the North African campaign.

q: Who is associated with the construction of Masjid-e-Dirar in Islamic historical accounts?
ans: Hypocrites of Madinah built it; Abu Amir al-Rahib is associated with instigating it
facts: • The account is discussed in connection with Qur'an 9:107–110.
It is more precise to say Abu Amir was associated with the plot rather than simplistically stating he personally built it.

q: When was Malala Yousafzai awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
facts: • Malala shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Kailash Satyarthi.
She was the youngest Nobel laureate at the time of the award. Primary / official reference

q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
facts: • A regular pentagon has five equal sides and five equal angles.
The sum of its interior angles is 540 degrees.

q: What is another name for K2?
facts: • K2 is the world's second-highest mountain above sea level, after Everest.
It lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan–China border region.

q: In which year were the Montagu–Chelmsford reforms enacted?
facts: • The Government of India Act 1919 implemented important parts of the reforms.
It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

q: Who opposed Ayub Khan in Pakistan's 1965 presidential election?
facts: • Fatima Jinnah was known as Madar-e-Millat.
Ayub Khan won the election through the Basic Democrats electoral college.

q: Where is the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant located?
ans: Near Chashma Barrage, Mianwali District, Punjab, Pakistan
facts: • Pakistan's Chashma units are operated under IAEA safeguards.
The plant is commonly abbreviated CHASNUPP; the site is in the Chashma/Kundian area. Primary / official reference

q: Which Companion served Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for about ten years?
facts: • Anas (RA) served the Prophet in Madinah after his mother brought him as a young boy.
He is an important narrator of hadith.

q: What is the upper house of Pakistan's Parliament called?
facts: • The lower house is the National Assembly.
Pakistan's Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses under Article 50 of the Constitution.

q: What was Hazrat Safiyyah's relationship to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
ans: Wife of the Prophet; Safiyyah bint Huyayy (RA)
facts: • She was one of the Mothers of the Believers.
She married the Prophet after the Battle of Khaybar according to traditional accounts.

q: Which is commonly called the world's highest battlefield?
facts: • The Siachen Glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram.
The glacier has been the site of a long-running India–Pakistan military deployment.

q: When was the United Nations founded?
facts: • The UN Charter entered into force on this date.
The Charter had been signed on 26 June 1945. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 85

q: What is the world's largest desert?
ans: Antarctic Desert (largest desert overall); Sahara is largest hot desert
facts: • Deserts are defined by low precipitation.
Antarctica is a polar desert despite being covered by ice.

q: What is the movement of people from one place to another called?
facts: • Migration may be internal or international.
Emigration means leaving a country; immigration means entering a country.

q: How many official copies of the Qur'an were prepared under Caliph Uthman (RA)?
ans: Traditional accounts commonly mention several standard copies sent to major centres; the exact total varies (often 5–7)
facts: • Uthman's recension helped standardize the written text and spelling tradition.
Avoid treating “seven copies” as universally agreed across all historical sources.

q: How many members were in Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly at its formation?
ans: 69 members is the common historical figure; later membership changed
facts: • The Constituent Assembly met for the first time on 10 August 1947.
Quaid-e-Azam was elected its first President/Speaker on 11 August 1947.

q: Which ordinal general election was Pakistan's 2018 general election in common post-1970 counts?
ans: The 11th general election (counting the nationwide general elections since 1970)
facts: • The 2018 election was held on 25 July 2018.
It resulted in PTI emerging as the largest party in the National Assembly.

q: Which Companion suggested digging a trench during the Battle of the Trench?
facts: • The battle is also called Ghazwa-e-Khandaq or the Battle of the Confederates.
It took place around Madinah in 5 AH / 627 CE.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
facts: • The UN also has major offices in Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.
The headquarters complex is on the East River in Manhattan. Primary / official reference

q: When was the Quit India Movement launched?
ans: 8 August 1942 (mass arrests and major actions began on 9 August)
facts: • The All-India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India resolution in Bombay.
Gandhi used the slogan “Do or Die.”

q: What is the deepest known point on Earth?
ans: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench
facts: • It is in the western Pacific Ocean.
Modern measurements put it at roughly 10.9–11 km below sea level, depending on the survey.

q: Where is the Shah Jahan Mosque located?
facts: • The mosque is famed for its geometric tile work and acoustics.
Do not confuse it with the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore.

q: From which country is UN Secretary-General António Guterres?
facts: • Guterres has served as the ninth UN Secretary-General since 1 January 2017, with his second term ending in 2026.

As of 14 October 2026 he remains in office; this current-affairs item should be updated if the next Secretary-General is appointed. Primary / official reference PRO GENIUS FORCES ACADEMY | PMA LONG COURSE Page 89

q: Where are the Black Hills located?
ans: South Dakota and Wyoming, United States; the prompt's “Black Mountain” wording is unclear
facts: • The Black Hills are a mountain range in the western Great Plains of North America.
The “Black Hills” are not a mountain range in Europe or Asia; check whether the original source meant a different feature.

q: How many Muslims were initially in the army at the Battle of Uhud?
ans: About 1,000 initially; after about 300 withdrew, roughly 700 remained
facts: • The withdrawal is associated with Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his followers in traditional accounts.
Many standard accounts say about 70 Muslims were killed at Uhud.

q: What is the capital of Algeria?
facts: • Algiers is a Mediterranean port city.
Algeria is Africa's largest country by area.

q: Who is often named as a founder of representative democracy in Pakistan?
ans: Muhammad Ali Jinnah is sometimes given in GK material, but “founder of democracy” is an imprecise title
facts: • Jinnah was Pakistan's founding Governor-General and advocated constitutional government.
Treat the phrase as an attribution/opinion rather than a formal historical office or uncontested title.

q: Which country is commonly described as the world's largest democracy?
facts: • India is the world's most populous democracy by population.
India has a parliamentary system with a President as head of state and Prime Minister as head of government.

q: When was NATO established?
facts: • The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington, D.C.
NATO originally had 12 members and has expanded since.

q: Who was the formal President of Cuba during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
ans: Osvaldo Dorticós Torrado; Fidel Castro was Prime Minister
facts: • The Cuban Missile Crisis occurred in October 1962.
This question tests the difference between formal head of state and the country's most prominent revolutionary leader.

q: Where is Nari Bolan Dam located?
facts: • The dam is located in the Nari/Bolan area.
It is distinct from Warsak Dam on the Kabul River and Tarbela Dam on the Indus. Primary / official reference

q: What did Pakistan's 1956 Constitution state about national/state languages?
ans: Urdu and Bengali were recognized as state languages; English could be used for official purposes during a transitional period
facts: • This provision reflected Pakistan's two wings before the 1971 separation.
Bengali became the national language of Bangladesh after independence.

q: In which district are the Khewra Salt Mines located?
facts: • Khewra is part of the Salt Range.
It is one of Pakistan's best-known salt mining and tourist sites. Primary / official reference

q: When was the Partition of Bengal annulled?
ans: 12 December 1911 was the announcement date; the reorganization took effect later
facts: • The partition had been made in 1905 under Lord Curzon.
The capital of British India was also announced to move from Calcutta to Delhi at the 1911 Delhi Durbar.

q: Who was the principal leader associated with the founding of the USSR?
ans: Vladimir Lenin; the USSR was formally established on 30 December 1922
facts: • The Soviet Union began as a union of Soviet republics after the Russian Revolution and civil war.
It dissolved in 1991.

q: When was Pakistan's first nationwide martial law imposed?
facts: • President Iskander Mirza proclaimed martial law and appointed General Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Ayub Khan removed Mirza from power later in October 1958.

q: Jinnah Barrage is built on which river?
ans: Indus River, near Kalabagh in Mianwali District
facts: • The barrage is used for irrigation diversion.
Do not confuse Jinnah Barrage with the proposed Kalabagh Dam, which is a separate project.
